title: Iran's parliament approves Mehrdad Akhlaqi as minister of defence
gist: Iran's parliament approved sanctioned defence-industry veteran Mehrdad Akhlaqi as defence minister, who pledged to rebuild military-industrial capacity and threatened the US over any use of the MOAB. CNN reported US strike plans against Iranian energy and nuclear sites could include the GBU-43/B.

insights.claim: Iran's parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as defence minister, ending months of interim leadership after Aziz Nasirzadeh was killed in US-Israeli strikes in February.
insights.so_what: Leadership normalization suggests Iran is consolidating its war-time institutions.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Akhlaqi has decades in Iran's defence industry including aerospace and missile roles, and is subject to US and EU sanctions.
insights.so_what: Missile-sector appointee signals focus on production and procurement.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Akhlaqi pledged to rebuild military-industrial infrastructure, accelerate defence technology, and expand cooperation with private-sector companies.
insights.so_what: Points to a rebuild of missile and drone capacity; relevant to regional risk persistence.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: CNN reported the US has developed strike plans, potentially using the GBU-43/B MOAB against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if Trump orders renewed combat operations.
insights.so_what: Renewed US strikes on energy infrastructure would be a major oil and gas risk event.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Akhlaqi warned that if Trump drops a single bomb, US troops would be carried out of the region, and said Tehran has taken measures to counter potential MOAB use.
insights.so_what: Rhetoric implies Iranian retaliation against US forces if strikes resume.
insights.quote: "If he drops a single bomb, he will have to see how many of his troops end up being carried out of the region in a horizontal position,"
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
